newsitem.title: USA: Taxpayers group sues San Diego, Calif., over fees.
newsitem.headline: Taxpayers group sues San Diego, Calif., over fees.

text.p: Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association sued City of San Diego for allegedly failing to comply with California's Proposition 218, approved by voters last November, officials said Tuesday.

The association said the San Diego lawsuit was the first of up to a dozen the group intended to file against local governments for alleged violations of the proposition, which requires voter approval of most local taxes and fees.
In the lawsuit, the taxpayers' group is targeting the special fees charged to business owners in San Diego to fund downtown and beach area improvements.
The city maintains that the fees were not subject to Proposition 218's strict vote requirements.
The association said it plans to file its second Proposition 218 lawsuit within the next two weeks. The association would not name the target.

"Most governments are complying with it (the proposition)," said Jonathan Coupal, the association's director of legal affairs. "But I would say a substantial minority of municipalities are violating Proposition 218 in one way or another."

Known as the Right to Vote on Taxes Act, Proposition 218 strengthened California law to require that all new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. The proposition called for property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limited the use of fees and charges.
Proposition 218 was designed to close loopholes in California's Proposition 13, which was also spearheaded by activists with the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association.
The passage in 1978 of Proposition 13 in California rolled back local property taxes and drastically curtailed the ability of counties to raise revenues to cover expenses.
